title: Dependency injection with Depends
summary: Depends declares that a parameter's value is provided by a function FastAPI runs before the handler, on every request.

sections.definition: Depends declares that a parameter's value is provided by a function that FastAPI runs before the handler, on every request. Dependencies can have their own dependencies (a tree), their result is cached within the same request, and if they use yield they run cleanup after responding.
sections.analogy: Mise en place: before the chef cooks, someone leaves the ingredients ready and measured. The chef doesn't go to the storeroom or wash the dishes at the end.
sections.problem: Without dependencies you repeat in every endpoint how to open the session, read the token or paginate, and you can't replace those pieces in tests.
sections.code:example:
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends
from sqlmodel import Session, select

def get_session():
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session              # tras la respuesta, se cierra

SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]

def paginacion(pagina: int = 1, tamano: int = 20) -> dict:
    return {"offset": (pagina - 1) * tamano, "limit": tamano}

PaginacionDep = Annotated[dict, Depends(paginacion)]

@app.get("/pedidos")
def listar_pedidos(session: SessionDep, pag: PaginacionDep) -> list[PedidoPublico]:
    consulta = select(Pedido).offset(pag["offset"]).limit(pag["limit"])
    return session.exec(consulta).all()
sections.bad:
session = Session(engine)       # global, compartida

@app.get("/pedidos")
def listar():
    return session.exec(select(Pedido)).all()

A session shared by all requests: mixed-up data and unclosed connections.
sections.good:
@app.get("/pedidos")
def listar(session: SessionDep):
    return session.exec(select(Pedido)).all()

One session per request, closed at the end and replaceable in tests.
sections.bridge:typescript: It resembles a TypeScript dependency injection container (like InversifyJS or tsyringe), but there are differences worth mentioning in the interview. Those containers resolve by type or token and usually hand out singletons. FastAPI resolves by function, runs it on every request, and its parameters can come from the request itself (query, headers, body). For tests, app.dependency_overrides ≈ jest.mock on a module.
sections.interview: Depends tells FastAPI that a parameter is produced by another function. FastAPI resolves the dependency tree before the handler, on every request, and caches the results within that request. With yield I can open and close resources like the database session. Unlike classic injection containers, there are no singletons by default nor resolution by type, and in tests I replace dependencies with dependency_overrides.
sections.myths:
• Writing Depends(get_session()) with parentheses: you pass the result, not the function.
  • Expecting a singleton: each request creates its own value.
  • Putting heavy business logic inside dependencies.
  • Not creating aliases with Annotated and repeating Depends(...) in every endpoint.

items.q: Two dependencies of the same endpoint ask for SessionDep. How many times does get_session run in that request?
options: Once per endpoint in the app
Just once when the app starts
items.why: FastAPI caches the result of each dependency within the same request.

options: It passes the result of calling the function, not the function
